messages:
vera: Heads-up: the int2 quant + speculative fastpath canary we spun up shows a higher speedup than expected but some regression on codebench BLEU and few convo QA items. want quick triage.

akhil: can you paste the canary config? which fallback/warmup profile did we use?

vera: deployed with: `redwoodctl deploy --model ember-13b-int2-q --speculative-rate 0.5 --fallback=late --kv-warmup=soft`

rachel: interesting combo. int2 is aggressive; speculative might amplify low-likelihood tokens. any token-level metrics yet?

vera: pulled a small A/B run (2k samples) while we ramp. raw summary: `spec=0.5`: median throughput +21.7%, code-BLEU delta -3.4, convo-acc -1.2. `spec=0.2`: throughput +9.8%, BLEU -0.9, convo-acc -0.3.

metrics-bot: quick-metrics (2k sample): spec=0.5 | median_latency=7.2ms | throughput=137t/s | codeBLEU=-3.4 | convAcc=-1.2

tom: do we have per-token KL or logit shift traces? looks like classic "speculative jump" where top-1 flips early and then model latches.

vera: yes. attached snippet from token-traces (condensed):
```
# token idx, kl(spec||base), top1_diff_prob
10, 0.12, -0.03
11, 0.34, -0.18   <-- big jump aligned with hallucination
12, 0.20, -0.05
```

akhil: that spike at 11 is telling. hypothesis: partially decoded speculative tokens introduce a biased prefix that the int2 quantization makes harder to recover from. int2 reduces softmax sharpness.

rachel: to test causality: propose three axis sweep: (Q) int2 vs int4 vs int4+fp16-kv, (S) spec rate 0.0/0.2/0.5, (F) fallback aggressive vs late. keep temp and topk identical.

vera: agree. also add deterministic replay: fix seed and enforce greedy-deterministic decoding (no sampling) to rule out RNG. we should capture top-5 logits every token.

tom: ops: please avoid full route ramp until we understand. set route default for `code` and `convo` to spec=0.0 for now.

deploy-bot: deploy action: ember-13b-int2-q spec-canary v2026.03.24 started (split=8%) on cluster-b at 2026-03-24T09:04:11Z.

vera: initial micro-sample of 20 failure cases shows consistent pattern: hallucination tokens often introduced right after longer prefix (>40 tokens) and correlate with low embed-sim to ground truth.

metrics-bot: example embed-cosine delta per request (spec vs base): mean_delta=-0.045, std=0.012.

akhil: two quick experiments to run in parallel:
- E1: same canary but `--kv-warmup=hard` (delay speculative until kv warmed)
- E2: int4 quant instead of int2 with same spec=0.5
Both should be cheap to run.

rachel: also add an instrumentation flag `runtime.emit_spec_origin=true` so we can tell whether a token was produced by the speculative path or produced after fallback. correlate that with errors.

vera: started E1 and E2 on a small fleet (5 nodes each). posting quick perf numbers as they come.

metrics-bot: E1 (kv-hard, spec=0.5, int2): throughput +16.3%, codeBLEU -1.4, convAcc -0.4
metrics-bot: E2 (int4, spec=0.5): throughput +18.9%, codeBLEU -0.8, convAcc -0.2

tom: E1 result suggests kv-warmup reduces the quality gap but costs some throughput. E2 shows int4 buys back quality with comparable speed.

vera: action items we agreed on:
- short-term: set sensitive routes to spec=0.0, default low-risk routes to spec=0.2.
- mid-term: add `emit_spec_origin`, `token_kl_trace`, `embed_delta` to eval harness and compute KL burst score per request.
- run full axis sweep (QxSxF) on 20k sample with deterministic replay and human micro-review of top 100 KL-burst requests.
- product: add perf-cost calc (delta cost/token) for int2+spec vs int4+spec.

akhil: +1. will draft experiment matrix and ownership. rachel/tom to own instrumentation changes. vera will run the sweep and curate microcases.

vera: will follow up with the curated 100 cases and the full 20k sweep results in this thread. thanks all. :rocket:
